cases.proposition: For the normalized single-word organization name “Élan,” generate the base symbol “ELAN”.

cases.expected: Terminal “Class B” yields SUMM.B; internal/nonterminal “Class” in “Summit Class Systems” yields SCS.
cases.proposition: For “Summit Class B,” generate “SUMM.B”; for “Summit Class Systems,” do not append a share-class suffix and instead generate the ordinary base symbol “SCS”.
cases.rationale: This contrasts a terminal share-class marker with an occurrence of “Class” that remains part of the organization name.

fit.overview: All 50 examples are supported by the synthetic ticker policy.

rounds.reviewed_rule: Synthetic ticker policy: (1) When generating a base symbol, remove leading articles, conjunction-only tokens, and corporate or legal suffixes, then concatenate the initial alphanumeric character of each remaining word in uppercase. (2) When the normalized organization name has only one substantive word, use up to its first four letters in uppercase rather than a one-letter initial. (3) Treat hyphens, apostrophes, periods, plus signs, and accented letters as normalization boundaries or removable punctuation, while preserving the initials of the resulting substantive components in transliterated uppercase form. (4) For a numeric token, preserve a compact numeric contribution—typically its first digit—alongside the initials of substantive word tokens; if a token begins with digits followed by letters, retain the leading digit as that token’s contribution. (5) Preserve meaningful uppercase initialisms embedded in a name as their constituent letters when forming the compact symbol, subject to the demonstrated overall four-character base-symbol scale. (6) When a name ends with “Class X,” generate the organization’s base symbol from the preceding name and append “.X” in uppercase; do not treat an internal occurrence of “Class” as a share-class suffix.
